questions.statement: Which adjective describes a very big object?
questions.context: Actividad de descripcion oral en la que cada estudiante presenta un objeto de su casa.

options.feedback: small means little in size and is the opposite of what the question asks for.
long measures the length along the object and not its overall size.
big means large and describes the overall size of an object.
old refers to how long a person has lived or how old a thing is, not to its size.

questions.explanation: Los adjetivos de tamano, edad y longitud se confunden con frecuencia porque en espanol el adjective pequeno tambien puede describir longitud. En ingles big y small miden tamano, long mide extension y old mide tiempo.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Look at the picture: the streets are shiny and everything feels damp. Which adjective fits?
questions.context: Ejercicio de descripcion de las condiciones de un dia de lluvia.

options.feedback: dry means the opposite of wet and contradicts the picture of wet streets.
wet describes something soaked or damp, which is exactly what the picture shows.
hot is a temperature sensation and does not describe how damp the street is.
clean speaks about the absence of dirt, not about dampness.

questions.explanation: Elegir un adjetivo a partir de una imagen exige relacionar la pista visual con la palabra. Las calles brillantes y la sensacion de humedad remiten a wet, mientras que las demas opciones describen condiciones que la imagen no presenta.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Read: "My grandfather gave me an old watch that still works." What is old in this sentence?
questions.context: Lectura de un texto breve sobre un objeto encontrado en la playa.

options.feedback: The question asks which element is old, and the word that names it on its own is not a complete answer.
The text qualifies the watch as old, and that complete phrase answers the question.
The grandfather is the one who gives the object, but the text does not say he is old.
The beach is not mentioned in the text, so it cannot be the old element.

questions.explanation: Los adjetivos se anaden al sustantivo que califican, y en una oracion con varios sustantivos es facil atribuir el adjetivo al equivocado. Localizar el sustantivo que sigue inmediatamente a old resuelve la pregunta sin ambiguedad.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the sentence that is correct.
questions.context: Ejercicio de produccion escrita para describir los utiles de un escritorio.

options.text: The book is red and small.
options.feedback: That sentence is grammatically correct, but the exercise asks for the option that best matches the prompt, and that is not this combination.

options.text: The books red and small is.
options.feedback: The word order is disturbed and the verb is cannot open the sentence.

options.text: The pencils are long and new.
options.feedback: The subject is plural, so it takes are, and both adjectives agree with it correctly.

options.text: A pencils are long and new.
options.feedback: The article a cannot go with a plural noun such as pencils.

questions.explanation: Una oracion descriptiva necesita concordancia entre sujeto y verbo y entre articulo y sustantivo. La opcion correcta cumple las dos reglas, mientras que las demas fallan en el orden de los elementos o en el numero del sujeto.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Read the label: "This jacket is new and it is not cheap." What does the label say about the price?
questions.context: Ejercicio de lectura de la etiqueta de una prenda de ropa en una tienda.

options.feedback: The text says the opposite with the negation not cheap, which means expensive.
Not cheap means expensive in this context, so the text does indicate that it is expensive.
free means at no cost and the text does not say the price is zero.
The second sentence of the label gives information about the price, so it is not unknown.

questions.explanation: Interpretar not cheap requiere reconocer la doble negacion semantica que produce el anglicismo. Esa comprension se comprueba mejor en espanol, donde no es posible decir que algo no es barato, y esa diferencia es justamente lo que la pregunta evalua.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which question would you ask to know the colour of an object?
questions.context: Actividad de reflexion escrita en la que los estudiantes describen su objeto preferido.

options.feedback: That question asks for the age of the object and not for its colour.
That question asks for the place of origin and does not describe how the object looks.
What colour is the way to ask for the colour of something in English.
That question asks for a quantity, and the prompt is looking for a visual property.

questions.explanation: Cada propiedad del objeto tiene su palabra interrogativa: What colour para el color, How old para la edad y How big para el tamano. Elegir la pregunta correcta es un paso previo a construir la oracion de respuesta.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence describes the correct comparison?
questions.context: Ejercicio de descripcion comparada entre dos objetos de uso escolar.

options.text: A pen is bigger than a pencil case.
options.feedback: A pen cannot be bigger than a pencil case, so the comparison is impossible.

options.text: A pencil case is bigger than a pen.
options.feedback: A pencil case really is bigger than a pen, and the comparative bigger is used correctly.

options.text: A pencil case is more big than a pen.
options.feedback: Comparatives in English are formed with -er or with more, but never with both at once.

options.text: A pencil case is the big than a pen.
options.feedback: The comparative is bigER and not big, because the -er form is used with short adjectives.

questions.explanation: Los comparativos en ingles tienen dos caminos: anadir -er en adjetivos cortos como big, o anteponer more con adjetivos largos como interesting. Mezclar ambas formas o usar el grado positivo es el error tipico cuando el espanol resuelve todo con el mismo termino.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Read: "This chair is made of wood and that cup is made of glass." What is the cup made of?
questions.context: Lectura de un articulo sobre los materiales con que se fabrican los objetos cotidianos.

options.feedback: The text says literally that that cup is made of glass.
Wood is the material of the chair according to the first part of the text.
Plastic is not mentioned in the text.
Metal does not appear in the sentence either, so it cannot be the answer.

questions.explanation: En un texto con dos objetos y dos materiales, el lector debe emparejar cada elemento con su pareja correspondiente. Confundir los pares es el error tipico, y el estrategia preventiva es subrayar cada pareja en cuanto aparece en el texto.
questions.subject: ingles
